rationale: The pain is acute and financially real — a 10x billing surprise from a single bot is a nightmare for a paying Vercel customer — and those customers demonstrably already spend money on hosting and adjacent security tools (Cloudflare WAF, etc.), so willingness to pay is credible. The buyer is a nameable SaaS team (5–50 engineers, paying Vercel Pro or Enterprise), which is a solid B2B ICP, but the solution space is already partially served by Cloudflare's free tier and Vercel's own firewall additions, so differentiation needs proof. Operational autonomy is borderline: a middleware package or SaaS shield layer could run mostly hands-off once deployed, but onboarding and configuration per customer may require engineering involvement — this needs to be validated before committing to build.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a zero-config bot-shield layer (an npm middleware package + a hosted SaaS tier) that blocks known cost-amplifying crawlers on Vercel/edge deployments and fires a cost-cap alert before the bill spirals. The factory builds it as a Claude-generated middleware script bundled with a landing page, a Stripe subscription link (e.g. $19/mo for cost-cap alerts, $49/mo for active blocking), and an email-based onboarding flow — no coding by the operator. Sell by posting in Vercel's community Discord, the r/vercel and r/nextjs subreddits, and replying to HN threads about unexpected cloud bills; outreach drafts are prepared by the factory and sent only after operator approval. Once installed, the middleware runs on the customer's deployment; billing and alerting run via Stripe + automated email (Claude-driven); the operator's only recurring touch is approving new outreach batches and reviewing monthly Stripe payouts. The honest caveat: buildability scores only a 5 here because packaging a reliable, battle-tested middleware that doesn't break customer apps requires careful integration work — the factory can scaffold it, but a first real customer install may surface edge cases that need a technical review.
notes: build_gate borderline: buildability_with_ai=5 is below the 6 floor, which is why the stage is capped at validate. Confirm the middleware can be made robust enough to ship without per-customer hand-holding before promoting to build.
